analysis_steps.goal: Make Stokes I, Q, U and polarization maps

method.value: Combine separately calibrated execution blocks and image with Briggs weighting; debias polarization intensity using Q and U noise

evidence.quote: The polarization intensity map achieved by the Stokes Q and U maps with a debias using the Stokes Q and U map noise level has a RMS noise of 0.008 mJy beam$^{-1}$.
Images were made using a Brigg’s weighting with a robust parameter of 0.5.

analysis_steps.goal: Infer B-field morphology and polarization fraction vs intensity

method.value: Rotate polarization by 90 deg to get B vectors; compare with outflow; plot Pfrac vs I and read power-law slopes

evidence.quote: In Figure [1](#fig_mag_out), we rotate the polarization directions by 90 degree and infer the magnetic fields.

assumptions.value: Grains aligned with magnetic fields; optical depth tau~0.2 at peak for T=30 K

evidence.quote: which corresponds to an optical depth $\tau \sim 0.2$ when assuming $T = 30$ K
Interestingly, Figure [4](#fig_pi) shows multiple slopes that encompass the limits of the distributions in a qualitative manner.

analysis_steps.goal: Estimate B-field strength with DCF and magnetic braking timescale

method.value: Smooth Q and U with 3x larger beam axes for background field, measure dispersion in 0.3-6.5 mJy/beam region, mass from dust continuum, apply DCF; Alfven speed and braking time

evidence.quote: we smoothed the Stokes Q and U maps with a nine-times larger beam (extended in both major and minor axes of the original beam by a factor of three)

findings_qualitative.value: Clear hourglass B field, poloidal outside and toroidal at the center, plus a clumpy depolarized strip perpendicular to the outflow

evidence.quote: poloidal in the outer regions and rapidly switching to toroidal in the inner region

claims.hypothesis: Does the B field change from outflow-aligned to a disk-like pattern on 100 au scales?
claims.result: Hourglass field with central toroidal-like pattern
claims.finding: Consistent with a toroidal field from a disk, though self-scattering or accretion-dragged fields are possible

evidence.quote: the central pattern is consistent with a toroidal field indicative of a circumstellar disk, although other interpretations are also possible

claims.hypothesis: Is the field strong enough to hinder disk formation?
claims.finding: Braking should be efficient, in tension with a central disk, implying non-ideal MHD or turbulence

evidence.quote: found that magnetic braking should be very efficient in the system, which is inconsistent with the strong hints of a central disk

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Self-scattering cannot be ruled out with Band 6 alone; accretion-dragged field considered less likely

evidence.quote: self-scattering cannot be ruled out by the data set taken only in Band 6

limitations_admitted.value: DCF very rough; no observed non-thermal linewidth; central mass uncertain

evidence.quote: We do not have an observational non-thermal linewidth

referee_caveats_inferred: DCF in a collapsing, outflow-affected region with assumed linewidth is highly uncertain
Band 6 alone cannot separate scattering from alignment
Slope regimes are not fitted quantitatively

reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: ~20-50 GB for two Band 6 polarization tracks
reproducibility.score_reason: Data are in the ALMA archive and the analysis is simple, but the calibration and imaging details are sparse.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Calibration, polarization processing and vector selection are not specified enough to redo the recipe reliably.
